text:
ashley_arch: RFC follow-up — quick sync on an "escape-hatch" and policy translation layer for canary/A-B rollouts. main tension: runtime-local fast decisions vs central durable signals for correctness. need to pick interfaces and failure modes.

ben_platform: +1. prefer router/runtime to own immediate fallback decisions (latency), central observer should supply consolidated signals (quality, latency, error-rate). avoid pushing fallback logic to clients.

maria_dev: curious about soft-degrade path vs hard rollback. customers have mixed SLOs; sometimes we want gradual degradation (smaller model or fewer tokens) before full cutover.

dave_oncall: from ops POV durability matters. if control plane flaps we need a local runway (autonomous fallback) to keep traffic flowing. soft-state only buys you minutes.

liam_infra: implementation idea: introduce route-level "fallback_budget" token bucket. runtime enforces per-window budget and will apply graded actions (quantized variant -> tiny model -> full fallback) until budget exhausted, then escalate to hard rollback.

ashley_arch: sketch for policy DSL (proposal):
```
policy {
  id: "rollout-2026-06"
  conditions: [latency_95p > 200ms for 2m, quality_delta > 0.8% for 5m]
  actions: [hedge(percentage=20, variant=v2-small), degrade(max_tok=128), fallback(variant=stable)]
  budget: {tokens: 1000, window: 1m}
}
```
Keep it compact, serializable, with explicit default-safe behavior.

maria_dev: we also need canonical telemetry keys: rollout.id, variant.id, budget.remaining, fallback.reason, signal.source. if not standardized, automation and alerts will be a mess.

ben_platform: edge case: multi-region rollouts where variant availability differs. question: who arbitrates cross-region decisions? suggestion: observer aggregates signals globally, router does final decision locally using policy + observer verdict. router must be able to fall back to region-compatible variants.

dave_oncall: noisy quality signals cause churn. recommend smoothing window + escalation counter. don't trigger global pager for transient noise.

maria_dev: agree. signal thresholding: require X consecutive windows or a weighted score from the eval-suite before auto-rollback. reuse existing eval-suite hooks to avoid inventing new thresholds.

deploy-bot: rollout 6280012345 started — model=gpt-x-lite variant=v2 canary=3% :rocket:

ashley_arch: storage choices: where to keep policy state? durable central KVS (etcd/consul) vs local redis with AOF. tradeoffs: recovery vs latency. thoughts?

liam_infra: pragmatic approach: keep live policy and budget counters local in redis (AOF enabled) for sub-100ms decisions, and checkpoint snapshots to central KVS every 30s. on restart, runtime rehydrates from latest checkpoint then reconciles with observer.

ben_platform: important: version the policy schema. runtime should ignore unknown fields and default to a conservative safe policy (full fallback). also provide a read-only policy API for the console and alerts.

maria_dev: operational playbook: when auto-fallback triggers create a short-lived incident (annotated with rollout.id, reason, metric deltas). page only if fallback == full or customer-impacting. otherwise add to the rollout audit log.

dave_oncall: :thumbsup: also add a manual escape-hatch in console: ability to set route.fallback=off for a route or tenant (with audit and TTL).

ashley_arch: follow-ups (action items):
- maria_dev: proto for the policy DSL and signal mapping list
- ben_platform: runtime decision API + telemetry tag contract
- liam_infra: redis AOF checkpoint strategy and restore plan
- dave_oncall: oncall playbook + paging thresholds
Let's do a 30m sync tomorrow 10:00 to walk the proto.

ben_platform: sgtm — I'll sketch a tiny gRPC surface for router->observer verdicts and post in the doc.

maria_dev: I'll enumerate the eval metrics and suggested thresholds.

deploy-bot: Canary progress update (t+1m): latency_95p +9ms, quality_delta +0.3% — no action triggered.

dave_oncall: noted, I'll keep a watch and escalate if we hit escalation_count>2.

ashley_arch: thanks everyone. we'll aim to keep the translation layer minimal and the runtime fail-safe by default.
